title: Corey Haines's A/B testing playbook: hypotheses, sample size, and a growth experiment program
summary: An agent playbook for designing statistically valid A/B tests and running experimentation as an ongoing growth engine. Covers hypothesis structure, sample size, metric selection, avoiding peeking, interpreting results, ICE prioritization, velocity targets, and documenting winners as reusable patterns.

principles.text: Start every test with a specific hypothesis grounded in data, not 'let's see what happens'.
principles.quote: Because [observation/data], we believe [change] will cause [expected outcome] for [audience]. We'll know this is true when [metrics].

principles.text: Test one variable at a time, or you won't know what worked.
principles.quote: Single variable per test. Otherwise you don't know what worked

principles.text: Pre-commit to sample size and never stop a test early on a peek; peeking creates false positives.
principles.quote: Looking at results before reaching sample size and stopping early leads to false positives and wrong decisions. Pre-commit to sample size and trust the process.

principles.text: Define a primary metric tied to business value, plus secondary and guardrail metrics that must not get worse.
principles.quote: Primary metric tied to business value. Secondary metrics for context. Guardrail metrics to prevent harm

principles.text: Prioritize the experiment backlog with ICE scoring and keep it deep, re-scoring monthly.
principles.quote: ICE Score = (Impact + Confidence + Ease) / 3. Run highest-scoring experiments first. Re-score monthly as context changes.

principles.text: Treat experimentation as a compounding asset: document every winner as a reusable pattern in a playbook and apply it elsewhere.
principles.quote: Individual tests are valuable. A continuous experimentation program is a compounding asset.
